title: Hantavirus infection: global overview and current situation in Spain

analysis.scope_and_question: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic RNA viruses with a worldwide distribution and the capacity to cause severe human disease. More than 40 hantavirus species have been identified, of which over 20 are known to be pathogenic to humans. Old World hantaviruses are classically associated with Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), whereas New World hantaviruses predominantly cause Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS), a condition characterized by rapid progression to respiratory failure, shock, and substantial mortality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review summarizes current knowledge on hantavirus biology, reservoirs, transmission, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, laboratory diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, and prevention, with particular emphasis on the situation in Spain.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human infection is usually acquired through the inhalation of aerosols contaminated with excreta from infected reservoir animals, primarily rodents, although person-to-person transmission has been demonstrated for the Andes virus. Diagnosis relies mainly on serological and molecular methods. No universally effective antiviral therapy is currently available for hantavirus disease, and management remains largely supportive, with intensive care and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation playing a crucial role in severe cases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Worldwide, hantavirus infections remain underdiagnosed because many cases are asymptomatic or present with nonspecific clinical manifestations. Evidence accumulated over the last three decades confirms the circulation of hantaviruses in Spain, both in animal reservoirs and in humans. Although clinically recognized disease remains uncommon, serological and ecological studies demonstrate that these infections are present in the country.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Continued surveillance, improved diagnostic awareness, and the development of effective preventive and therapeutic strategies remain important public health priorities.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides a global overview of hantavirus infections, focusing on their biology, transmission, epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, with particular emphasis on the situation in Spain. Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic RNA viruses causing severe diseases like HFRS and HCPS. Human infection typically occurs through inhalation of aerosols from infected rodents, though person-to-person transmission has been observed with Andes virus. Diagnosis relies on serological and molecular methods, but no universally effective antiviral therapy exists, with management being largely supportive. Despite underdiagnosis due to asymptomatic or nonspecific cases, evidence confirms hantavirus circulation in Spain. Continued surveillance, improved diagnostic awareness, and development of preventive and therapeutic strategies are critical public health priorities.

title: Cruise-linked Andes virus and severe hantavirus lung disease: A narrative review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak, examining its transmission dynamics, clinical presentation, and implications for maritime travel medicine. The central question concerns the characteristics and management of this rare travel-associated zantavirus event.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the ANDV outbreak, including its biology, transmission, clinical features, diagnostics, and management. The review does not specify databases, search dates, or study counts, as it is a narrative synthesis rather than a systematic review.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: As of July 2026, 13 cases (12 confirmed, 1 probable) were reported, with 3 deaths. Transmission was likely land-based before embarkation, with limited onboard human-to-human spread, and was contained after a 42-day follow-up period. Severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome progresses rapidly, requiring intensive supportive care.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights preparedness gaps in shipboard triage, contact tracing, specimen transport, genomic surveillance, risk communication, and cross-border follow-up. No licensed antiviral therapy or vaccine is available, and the outbreak underscores challenges in early recognition and management.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening One Health-informed pre-travel counseling, post-travel symptom surveillance, and maritime outbreak protocols is essential. Improved coordination for zoonotic threats in expedition travel is needed, along with enhanced diagnostic and management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus outbreak, a rare travel-associated zoonotic event with 13 cases (12 confirmed, 1 probable) and 3 deaths. Transmission likely occurred before embarkation, with limited onboard spread, and was contained after 42 days. Severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome progresses rapidly, requiring intensive supportive care due to the lack of licensed antivirals or vaccines. The outbreak reveals critical gaps in shipboard preparedness, including triage, contact tracing, and genomic surveillance. Future priorities include strengthening One Health-informed pre-travel counseling, post-travel surveillance, and maritime outbreak protocols to address zoonotic threats in expedition travel.

title: Hantavirus risk and preparedness in Europe in an era of climate change and global mobility.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hantavirus epidemiology, ecology, and clinical recognition, diagnostics, and preparedness in Europe, with emphasis on endemic Puumala virus (PUUV), Dobrava virus (DOBV), and Seoul virus (SEOV), and clarifies the relevance of imported Andes virus (ANDV) infection for travel medicine and maritime response.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A structured narrative review of literature published from January 2000 to May 2026, prioritising surveillance reports, systematic and narrative reviews, rodent ecology studies, diagnostic evaluations, external quality assessment studies, and outbreak investigations. WHO, ECDC, and International Health Regulations guidance documents were also reviewed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: European hantavirus epidemiology is heterogeneous and shaped by reservoir ecology, biome-specific rodent dynamics, clinical awareness, diagnostic capacity, and surveillance practice. Climate effects are indirect and regionally variable, mediated by mast years, predator-prey dynamics, winter conditions, land use, reservoir density, and human exposure.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Diagnostic preparedness is uneven, particularly for molecular detection. Imported ANDV infection is rare in Europe but relevant to travel medicine and high-consequence preparedness because it can cause severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and, unlike endemic European hantaviruses, has documented person-to-person transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: European preparedness should prioritise PUUV, DOBV, and SEOV through rodent biomonitoring, harmonised surveillance, improved molecular diagnostics, and locally calibrated early warning. The 2026 MV Hondius cruise-ship cluster of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) infections has highlighted urgent gaps in European preparedness for both endemic and imported hantavirus disease.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines hantavirus risk and preparedness in Europe, focusing on endemic viruses (PUUV, DOBV, SEOV) and imported ANDV. It highlights heterogeneous epidemiology shaped by rodent ecology, climate effects, and diagnostic disparities. Key gaps include uneven molecular diagnostic capacity and the need for improved preparedness for imported ANDV, which can cause severe disease and person-to-person transmission. Recommendations include rodent biomonitoring, harmonised surveillance, and early warning systems tailored to local conditions.

title: A historical cross-border Andes virus lineage reveals the origin of a cruise ship hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the origin and evolutionary history of the Andes virus responsible for a multi-country outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome among passengers and crew of a cruise ship in 2026.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed complete ANDV small (S), medium (M), and large (L) genome segment sequences from Chile alongside outbreak-associated and publicly available genome sequences to trace the geographic origin of the outbreak-associated virus.
analysis.methods: Complete ANDV genome segment sequences from Chile were analyzed alongside outbreak-associated and publicly available sequences, and phylogeographic analysis was performed to determine the genetic relationship and geographic origin of the outbreak virus.
analysis.main_results: The outbreak virus clustered within an ANDV Clade III cluster spanning southern Chile and northern Patagonia in Argentina and was most closely related to a human-derived ANDV collected in Los Rios Region of Chile in 2012; phylogeographic analysis showed that the genetically distinct ANDV Clade V lineage circulating in central Chile was not closely related to the cruise ship outbreak-associated genomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings trace the geographic origin of the outbreak-associated virus to a defined corridor, the Hua Hum Pass, a cross-border zone connecting Neuquen Province in Argentina with the Los Rios and La Araucania Regions of Chile, representing a novel identification of the outbreak's origin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide critical information for surveillance and prevention efforts by identifying the specific geographic region where the outbreak virus originated, which can help in targeting public health interventions to prevent future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is high as it is based on complete genome sequence analysis and phylogeographic analysis, but limitations include the potential for incomplete sampling of viral strains in the region and the reliance on publicly available sequences which may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the origin and evolutionary history of the Andes virus responsible for a 2026 cruise ship outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. By analyzing complete ANDV genome sequences from Chile alongside outbreak-associated sequences, researchers found the outbreak virus clustered within ANDV Clade III, closely related to a 2012 human-derived strain from Chile's Los Rios Region. Phylogeographic analysis traced the outbreak's origin to the Hua Hum Pass, a cross-border zone between Argentina and Chile. This identification of the specific geographic corridor provides critical insights for surveillance and prevention efforts, though the study's strength is tempered by potential sampling limitations and reliance on publicly available sequences.

title: The MV Hondius Hantavirus Outbreak—Lessons for Pandemic Preparedness

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, examining how it exposed weaknesses in global health preparedness and proposing reforms to enhance operational authority and coordination across jurisdictions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a Perspective article that analyzes the outbreak through a narrative synthesis of available evidence, without reporting specific study designs, populations, or meta-analytic methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the hantavirus outbreak highlighted critical gaps in pandemic preparedness, particularly in international coordination and response mechanisms, and emphasizes the need for systemic reforms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a lack of standardized protocols for cross-jurisdictional coordination and limited data on the effectiveness of current response strategies, which remain unresolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests the need for improved surveillance systems, enhanced communication frameworks, and updated guidelines for managing outbreaks of hantaviruses and similar pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This review analyzes the hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, emphasizing its role in exposing vulnerabilities in global health preparedness. It outlines the need for reforms in operational authority and cross-jurisdictional coordination. The review is a narrative synthesis of available evidence, highlighting gaps in standardized protocols and data on response effectiveness. It proposes specific research and practice implications, including improved surveillance and updated guidelines for managing hantavirus outbreaks and similar pathogens.

title: Omics Approaches in Hantavirus Research: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives

analysis.scope_and_question: Hantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses responsible for two severe human diseases: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review summarizes genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and AI-enabled approaches in hantavirus research.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Although single-layer genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics studies have advanced our understanding of hantavirus biology, true multi-omics integration remains scarce, leaving systems-level mechanisms of disease severity and host–pathogen interactions unresolved.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Proteomics has revealed host proteins involved in immune regulation, endothelial dysfunction, and potential therapeutic targeting, whereas metabolomics indicates substantial metabolic reprogramming during infection, although dedicated studies remain limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: AI-based approaches are increasingly applied to outbreak prediction, surveillance, and risk modeling. Drawing on successful multi-omics frameworks developed for other viral infections, we discuss opportunities to improve biomarker discovery, surveillance, therapeutic development, and future precision medicine strategies for hantavirus infections.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the application of omics technologies in hantavirus research, focusing on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches. Hantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses causing severe human diseases such as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). While single-layer omics studies have enhanced understanding of viral biology, multi-omics integration is still limited, leaving unresolved systems-level mechanisms of disease severity and host–pathogen interactions. Proteomics has identified host proteins involved in immune regulation and endothelial dysfunction, but metabolomics studies are still limited. AI-based methods are increasingly used for outbreak prediction and risk modeling, and the review highlights opportunities for improving biomarker discovery, surveillance, and therapeutic development for hantavirus infections.

title: Bile acid signaling at the gut–vascular interface: a novel modulator of hantavirus endothelial barrier dysfunction

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus infection causes life-threatening hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) due to severe endothelial barrier breakdown, with clinical severity varying widely and no targeted endothelial-protective treatments available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study synthesized four core lines of evidence from metagenomic reports, re-analysis of three public GEO datasets (GSE245916, GSE7271, GSE270172), and experimental findings on FXR/TGR5 agonists and HTNV effects.
analysis.methods: Researchers re-analyzed public GEO datasets via standardized RNA-seq/microarray pipelines, examined endothelial cell receptor expression, tested FXR/TGR5 agonists in inflammation and vascular injury models, and investigated HTNV's impact on cholesterol metabolism and bile acid precursors.
analysis.main_results: SEOV-infected human/rat lung endothelial cells showed conserved VCAM1/ICAM1 upregulation; SEOV-infected rat lung displayed sustained Nfkb1 suppression and Slc10a2 downregulation; PUUV 3D vessel chips featured IL6 elevation and disrupted BA transporters; TGR5 was undetectable in endothelial cells; FXR/TGR5 agonists repressed NF-κB inflammation and mitigated lung vascular injury; HTNV upregulated CH25H to block HMGCR-dependent cholesterol synthesis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors propose a unified pathogenic model where hantavirus-triggered gut dysbiosis and impaired cholesterol metabolism deplete circulating FXR/TGR5 agonistic bile acids, relieving inhibition of endothelial NF-κB and monocyte NLRP3 inflammasomes to exacerbate capillary leakage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The gut microbiota–bile acid–FXR/TGR5 axis represents a repurposable therapeutic target for hantavirus diseases, offering a testable roadmap for clinical multi-omics cohorts, in vitro receptor modulation assays, and in vivo pharmacological interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Direct causal evidence connecting bile acid signaling to viral vascular damage remains absent, though the evidence strength is high due to the integration of multiple datasets and experimental findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates hantavirus-induced endothelial barrier dysfunction by examining the role of bile acid signaling. The authors synthesized evidence from metagenomic reports, re-analysis of public datasets, and experimental work, showing that hantaviruses disrupt gut microbiota and cholesterol metabolism, leading to depletion of FXR/TGR5 agonistic bile acids. This loss removes constitutive inhibition of NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasomes, exacerbating capillary leakage. The study identifies the gut microbiota–bile acid–FXR/TGR5 axis as a novel therapeutic target, though direct causal evidence is still needed. The findings provide a framework for future validation through clinical, in vitro, and in vivo studies.

title: Hantavirus ditemukan pada peternak satwa liar di Vietnam: Alarm bagi Asia Tenggara

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate hantavirus exposure among wildlife farmers in Vietnam, addressing a knowledge gap about zoonotic disease risks in this high-risk occupation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 210 wildlife farmers in Lao Cai and Dong Nai provinces, Vietnam, between August 2023 and March 2024.
analysis.methods: Researchers tested farmers for hantavirus antibodies to determine prior exposure and current infection status, focusing on those exclusively involved in wildlife farming without hunting or processing activities.
analysis.main_results: 8.7% of wildlife farmers tested positive for hantavirus antibodies, indicating prior exposure, while 1.9% had suspected recent infections during the study period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that wildlife farming itself poses a significant hantavirus risk independent of direct animal handling, highlighting an underrecognized transmission pathway.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Results emphasize the need for enhanced surveillance and biosecurity measures in wildlife farms across Southeast Asia to prevent zoonotic hantavirus transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the large sample size and targeted population provide moderate evidence for occupational risk assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated hantavirus exposure among 210 wildlife farmers in Vietnam, finding 8.7% had antibodies indicating prior infection and 1.9% had suspected recent infections. The research reveals that wildlife farming itself poses significant hantavirus risk independent of direct animal handling, suggesting an underrecognized transmission pathway. These findings highlight the need for enhanced surveillance and biosecurity measures in wildlife farms across Southeast Asia to prevent zoonotic disease spread.

title: Metatranscriptomics reveals urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap of limited systematic comparisons of virome compositions across urbanization gradients by investigating urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted large-scale sampling in two densely populated Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, with distinct climates, collecting 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans.
analysis.methods: Metagenomic sequencing was used to analyze the rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents, enabling identification of vertebrate-associated viruses and assessment of their zoonotic potential.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43), and discovered two viruses previously unreported in rodents.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as revealing cross-order transmission risk and highlighted the importance of spatial distance in shaping the distribution and transmission of rodent-borne viruses, with meteorological variables independently explaining 5.0% of the variation in viral community composition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights are essential for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments, particularly for viruses with zoonotic potential like Orthohantavirus seoulense.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it provides comprehensive virome data but may have limitations in generalizability beyond the sampled cities and rodent species.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities using metagenomic sequencing. Sampling 1,072 rodents from four species in Wuhan and Shenzhen, the researchers identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and HCoV_OC43). They also discovered two previously unreported rodent viruses, revealing cross-order transmission risks. The analysis showed that meteorological variables explained 5.0% of viral community composition divergence between cities. These findings highlight the importance of spatial distance in virus distribution and provide critical insights for proactive surveillance and mitigation of zoonotic threats in urban environments.
